chats.answer:
For a 16-inch MacBook Pro, I'd buy the espresso Pro 15 if price isn't a major constraint. Its 4K resolution gives you crisp text beside the MacBook's Retina display, it's bright enough for most work environments, and its adjustable stand makes a two-screen setup much more comfortable. For most people spending their own money, though, I'd choose a less expensive 2.5K display. 
RTINGS.com
+1

My picks

espresso Pro 15 — Best overall

15.6-inch 4K IPS, 60Hz, 550 nits, USB-C. Excellent text clarity, macOS touch support and a flexible magnetic stand. Expensive, glossy and relatively power-hungry. 
RTINGS.com
+1

Arzopa Z3FC — Best value

16.1-inch 2.5K, up to 180Hz, about 1.7 lb. A good size match for your MacBook, with sharper text than 1080p and smooth scrolling. My practical pick for coding, browsers and office work. 
TechRadar
+1

ViewSonic VX1655-4K-OLED — Best picture

$499.99

ViewSonic

15.6-inch 4K OLED, 60Hz, about 1.5 lb. Deep blacks and excellent contrast make it appealing for photos and video. OLED burn-in risk makes it less attractive for all-day static code windows. 
PCWorld

Lenovo ThinkVision M14d — Best compact option

$253.00

Walmart - TheStore

14-inch, 2240×1400, matte IPS, USB-C. Its 16:10 aspect ratio is useful for documents, and it's easier to fit on a small café table. Noticeably smaller than your MacBook.

What matters specifically for your MacBook

I'd prioritize resolution over almost everything else. A 16-inch 1080p portable monitor will look visibly coarse beside your MacBook Pro. A 2560×1600-class screen is a good compromise; 4K is better for Retina-like text when using macOS's scaled display modes.

USB-C video and power over one cable is also worth having, but it drains the MacBook's battery. Don't assume a monitor's pass-through charging can supply enough power for a 16-inch Pro under heavy load. And if you love the MacBook's 120Hz ProMotion display, remember that most premium 4K portable monitors are limited to 60Hz.

Bottom line: Get the espresso for premium text clarity and ergonomics, or the Arzopa for value. I assumed this is primarily a travel productivity setup, rather than a color-critical HDR workstation. I haven't tested these side by side myself, and I couldn't verify current retail offers for those two models.

chats.answer:
For a 16-inch MacBook Pro, I’d buy the LG gram +view 16 for everyday work. It’s a similarly sized, 16:10 USB-C screen, so it feels natural beside the MacBook rather than like a smaller, wider accessory. If your priority is matching the MacBook’s exceptionally sharp text, I’d spend more on a 4K display.

Best picks

LG gram +view 16 (16MR70)

$249.99

LG

Best overall. 16-inch, 2560×1600 IPS, 16:10, wide color gamut, USB-C and included folio stand. Excellent for coding, documents and travel. Text won't be as crisp as on your MacBook.

ViewSonic VX1655-4K-OLED

$499.99

B&H Photo

Best image quality for the money. 15.6-inch 4K OLED, excellent contrast and color, built-in kickstand and USB-C. Sharper than the LG, but 16:9, glossy and limited to 60Hz. 
ViewSonic Global

SOTSU FlipAction Elite 16

$670.65

Walmart - SOTSU

Best premium productivity match. Its 3840×2400 resolution combines high pixel density with the MacBook's 16:10 proportions. Aluminum construction and an integrated folding stand; expensive and only 60Hz.

SOTSU FlipAction Pro 16 Gen 2

$509.15

B&H Photo

Best for smooth scrolling. 2560×1600 at 120Hz, with a folding, rotating stand. A good companion to a ProMotion MacBook if motion matters more than 4K text sharpness.

What matters specifically for your MacBook

The resolution is the biggest decision. A 2560×1600 screen gives you useful workspace at a reasonable price, but you'll notice the difference when dragging text from the MacBook onto it. A 3840×2400 screen can use clean 2× scaling to look like 1920×1200, producing very crisp text at a comfortable size. That's why the SOTSU Elite is my premium pick.

All four offer USB-C connectivity. Use a video-capable USB-C cable, and expect a bus-powered monitor to shorten your MacBook's battery life. Also, don't assume a monitor's USB-C charging passthrough can fully power a 16-inch MacBook Pro under heavy load.

Bottom line: LG for value; SOTSU Elite if you want a second screen that feels closer to the MacBook's display. I assumed you primarily want a travel-friendly productivity setup, rather than a color-reference or gaming monitor. I haven't tested these side by side, and the listed prices may change.
